content.title: Iraq to face Bolivia on March 31 for FIFA World Cup spot
content.text: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Bolivia overcame Suriname 2-1, paving the way for a crucial playoff against Iraq for a place in the FIFA World Cup 2026. The South American side will now meet Iraq on Tuesday, March 31, in Monterrey, Mexico, with both sides just one victory away from claiming a coveted berth in football’s greatest championship. Suriname, meanwhile, had their chances of reaching the finals for the first time dashed after giving up an early second-half lead. For Iraq, the match is a watershed moment in their campaign to reach the World Cup since 1986. The squad has been stepping up its training in recent days, concentrating on tactical discipline and defensive organisation ahead of what is likely to be a physically taxing match against Bolivia. The coaching staff led by Graham Arnold has been working hard to enhance the squad’s transition play and offensive efficiency, which are crucial for dismantling Bolivia’s sturdy system. Fitness has also been a top emphasis, with players enduring strenuous training sessions to ensure they can sustain their energy throughout the match in the circumstances predicted in Mexico. Iraq will want to build on their recent momentum with a combination of veteran internationals and rising prospects. The national team recognizes the gravity of the situation, with players and coaches stressing calm and concentration as critical components in such a high-pressure playoff. The winner of Tuesday’s match will move to Group I of the World Cup, where they will face a formidable battle. The qualifying squad will play France, Norway, and Senegal, a strong lineup with little room for mistake. With everything on the line, Iraq will try to rise to the occasion and complete the last step before returning to the world scene. Discover moreSportsSoccerSports memorabilia
